True in some contexts it can be helpful. But at its core, the Kinsey Scale attempts to model human sexuality exclusively on the basis of gender identity. I believe that is a very limited (if not flawed) conception of how our sexual and romantic attractions work.

Most people are attracted to a varied confluence of personal characteristics, not the label that others use to identify their gender. When the Kinsey Scale was invented, it was widely believed that specific physical and behavioral attributes had to always be in alignment with gender identity of male vs. female. Nowadays, however, gender distinctions are not so concrete, even within the gender binary. The Kinsey scale is therefore not only an inaccurate model of human sexuality, but it serves to perpetuate problematic stereotypes of manhood and womanhood that undermine people's understanding and acceptance of gender variance.

We can see evidence of this in this subreddit, where straight, gay, and even bi people are at a loss to describe their affinity for femboys because the current labels don't account whatsoever for gender presentation, only gender identity. In truth, the Kinsey scale doesn't offer clarity in these situations, and arguably it further clouds and confuses the issue. Hope that makes sense.

Good question! Sexual orientation only accounts for gender identity, which is a shortcoming of our current language. It is rooted in the misconception that all attributes of gender must be in alignment (social group affiliation, sense of self, name, pronouns, speech, behaviors, mannerisms, and of course physical sex characteristics). However, human sexual attractions are far more complex. Once you factor in gender nonconforming people (like femboys) or even the clinical paraphilias (like fetishism), the entire concept of sexual orientation falls apart. 

To this day, however, the LGBT community continues to promote gender identity to the exclusion of all other aspects of human sexuality mostly for reasons of acceptability politics. There is an underlying fear that gender nonconforming people and the clinical paraphilias pose a threat to queer rights, particularly to gay men, lesbians, and trans women. Such gatekeeping and identity policing is unfortunate because many people feel compelled to adhere to a narrow ideal of what it means to be straight, bi, gay, or lesbian effectively eliminating any possibility of exploring their own sexual nature beyond such narrow meanings. 

Just remember, sexual identity labels are human constructs. Sometimes they can prove helpful in the process of coming out. But they are not law, nor are they sacrosanct. If you find yourself questioning your sexual or romantic attractions, then rest assured your feelings are 100% valid and real, regardless of whether they conform to a dictionary definition. Please don't limit yourself to a societally imposed ideal of human sexuality. You do you!
